waterways.name: Southern Ocean
waterways.outlet: Encircles Antarctica; mixes with Atlantic, Pacific, and Indian Oceans
countries: Antarctica (no permanent countries; claimed sectors by several states)

facts.text: The ocean that completely surrounds Antarctica, recognized as the fifth ocean by many authorities.
Dominated by the Antarctic Circumpolar Current, the world’s strongest ocean current.
Drake Passage between South America and Antarctica is a classic rough-water trivia landmark.
Pub-trivia shorthand: the ring ocean — Drake Passage is the choke point west of the peninsula.
A deep bay of the Southern Ocean bounded by the Ross Ice Shelf, Earth’s largest ice shelf.
Home to McMurdo Station, the largest Antarctic research base (U.S.-operated).
Pub-trivia shorthand: ice-shelf sea of Antarctica’s Pacific-facing side.
Sea east of the Antarctic Peninsula; famous from Shackleton’s Endurance voyage.
Pub-trivia shorthand: Endurance shipwreck sea beside the peninsula.

waterways.name: Drake Passage
waterways.outlet: Connects Atlantic and Pacific south of South America

facts.text: The open-water gap between Cape Horn and the South Shetland Islands / Antarctic Peninsula.
Shortest crossing from South America to Antarctica; notoriously rough seas.
Ushuaia, Argentina, is a common gateway port for Drake Passage Antarctic cruises.
Pub-trivia shorthand: stormy gateway from South America to Antarctica.
